correctness.rationale: As t-modules, R=F_q[t]/(t^n) and W=F_q^r with tW=0 give diagonal blocks f,D and off-diagonal maps t^(n−1)b and evaluation at zero times c. Their lower-right cross product vanishes since n≥2, while their upper-left cross product is t^(n−1)bc. The constant term forces f(0)=0; the remaining equations are D²=0, bD=Dc=0 and f²+t^(n−1)bc=0. The flag im D=U⊆K=ker D and the induced isomorphism W/K→U yield exactly G_{r,k}; b descends to (K/U)* on restriction and c to K/U, each with q^k lifts. The first nonzero coefficient of f², when present, is the square of the first nonzero coefficient of f at twice its degree. For n=2h this forces valuation at least h and bc=0; for n=2h+1 it leaves only the equation a_h²+bc=0. In both cases the higher free coefficients give q^h. On a quotient of dimension s>0, a nonzero form has q^(s−1) vectors in every pairing fiber, while the zero form gives q^s vectors and forces a_h=0 when relevant. This produces the stated H factors, both equal to 1 at s=0, and their difference is (q−1)q^(s−1)(q^s−1) for positive s. The k=0 term gives strictness for r≥1; no square-root count or characteristic assumption is used. Centralizer size follows from n+2r+r² free coordinates. Independent spot replay enumerated all d×d matrices over each listed prime field by base-q expansion and filtered by ordinary matrix products XB=BX and X²=0: for (n,r,q)=(2,1,3),(3,1,2),(2,2,2), the centralizer sizes and square-zero counts were (243,15),(64,8),(1024,44). The all-parameter decision rests on the proof; the frozen checker and recorded output were inspected but not executed.
residual_risks: The independent spot replay is finite and did not include extension fields; the algebraic argument covers them, including characteristic two.
The formula is for n≥2 and counts labelled elements, not conjugacy classes.

evidence: The n=2 analysis enforces pairing zero on K/U. The r=1 odd analysis sees a scalar square plus a one-dimensional pairing, with D necessarily zero. The general odd tail requires controlling the surviving degree n−1 term simultaneously with the positive-rank tail D and all its pairing fibers.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Unifying the known slices is not just a parameter substitution: for odd n the lowest functorial square coefficient survives in degree n−1, and the rank-dependent dimension and lift factors matter simultaneously. The proof must derive the reduced equation and count q^(2s) solutions for each s, including s=0, across all ranks. That supplies the all-r comparison, which the slices and abstract encodings do not themselves establish.

originality.rationale: The credited distinct content is the all-tail count and normalized parity separation for a long hook, especially the odd n≥3, r≥2 fiber. Resultary 0260ec1ac7b2 already gives (and rank-refines) n=2, and 50a5542dfb83 already gives the r=1 parity family and more rank information there. The even normalized generalization is effectively the n=2 count after extracting free coefficients; neither overlap evaluates the odd hook when the square-zero tail can have positive rank. Inspected primary frameworks encode the counting problem or classify possible types, but do not give a theorem that evaluates this mixed pairing and valuation fiber. Pass is best of available evidence for the general result, not originality of the subcases or of the flag factor.
residual_risks: A more general evaluated representation-counting formula, including under Hall or quiver terminology, could imply the general claim; none was established in the inspected passages.
Targeted passages and indexed statements are not an exhaustive historical survey. The special cases identified above are existing coverage regardless of the relationship between records.

value.rationale: The natural finite-field fiber is determined for every rank of the square-zero tail block, and its size exhibits a strict residual parity gap after the free long-block coordinates are divided out. This separates parity from simple dimension growth and gives the probability of square-zero for a uniform commuting matrix. In the previously uncovered mixed regime it is an exact invariant of the hook centralizer, including characteristic two, rather than a tiny test instance or re-enumeration of the two known boundary slices.
